author: GamingBolt
description:
Starfield is nearly upon the PlayStation world, bringing not only a new expansion in Terran Armada but also a meaty update in Free Lanes (on top of previous patches). Available today, it can be an overwhelming experience, especially if you're brand-new to the Settled Systems, but don't worry. 

We'll dive into some of the best starting options, which planets you should visit first, and, perhaps more importantly, a few ways to prepare for the new content. Let's start with...
title: 15 Things Starfield PS5 Players Should Do First

author: GamingBolt
description: Starfield has finally arrived on PlayStation 5, going along with a significant new update in the form of Free Lanes, allowing Bethesda Game Studios to deliver the fullest and most polished version of its space faring RPG. Though this is by no means Starfield 2.0, Free Lanes allows the sci fi RPG to put its best foot forward in a way that it hasn't been able to before. All told, for PlayStation players who enjoy the space opera aesthetic or the Bethesda RPG formula, Starfield is a solid experience well worth investing time in.
title: Starfield PS5 Review - The Final Verdict (Still A Masterclass)

author: GamingBolt
description:
The second expansion released for Bethesda's space faring RPG doesn't do things much differently from the first, delivering a healthy chunk of new gameplay content that is ultimately more of the same. 

But though not exceptional, thanks to a compelling new faction, captivating new lore, and some interesting new gameplay additions, the Terran Armada expansion nonetheless does have its strengths. For players who have already invested a lot of time into Starfield and enjoyed its offerings, Terran Armada is a solid new addition.
title: Starfield Terran Armada DLC Review - The Final Verdict

author: GamingBolt
description:
I know, I know. “It's been almost three weeks,” you say, and I can't help but not talk about Crimson Desert. More of a testament to the sheer number of things there are to discuss about this massive not-so-hidden gem, this behemoth that's overtaken all conversation. Between the sheer attention to detail, the players who are still in Hernand (you guys know there's a desert in this game, right?), and those finding all kinds of crazy things that no one could have expected, it's a lot to unpack. And it's matched with a similar enthusiasm from the development team, who have been incredibly quick (and/or physically/emotionally taxed) to address the most important feedback.

So believe me when I say that it feels a little bad to point out something that really breaks the game. No, not in a fun, boss-deleting way like infinite explosive arrows, but a major design flaw. What makes it even crazier is that you won't notice it until you're already dozens of hours in.
title: Crimson Desert Has One MASSIVE Problem No One Is Talking About
